items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: He was a slick guy and it was very hard to get a decent salary from him. His idea was to have me to play with a bunch of young French amateurs who had formed a group not long ago. He wanted me to try to repeat the same experience that Sydney Bechet had made with Claude Luther and his group.

ctx.x: Other people used to stop and listen to these two young men play. The oldest one was better than the younger one and I suppose the reason was that he had more experience, but the younger one was no amateur although I found out that they did not read music. There were many pianists in those days that did not read music but had a natural talent for that instrument. They made their living playing for parties most of the time.

Another event that used to take place on Kenyon Avenue, was a jug band that used to come around often and play in the streets and pass around a hat for people to put money in. There was a harmonica player, a big glass jug that one fellow would blow in and make it sound like a bass, and a violin player named Luther who could make his violin sound like it was saying "Oh Luther"...They made good money because everyone enjoyed their music and gave freely whatever they could afford.

There was a family by the name of James that lived a few doors from me that had a piano player. The son, who was about my age, and I used to play together and I would go to his house very often and play the different piano rolls for hours. Many people who could not play music had these type of pianos..I loved music but never tried to play the piano at that time.
